title: Platform systems & services  team wiki, dashboards, runbooks, alerts and Q4 roadmap
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This page is the central platform engineering team wiki for our systems and services inventory, standard how-tos, dashboards & alerts guidance, runbooks for common incidents, recent retrospectives, and the Q4 roadmap. It is intended to be the canonical operational starting point for oncall, SREs, and platform engineers.

Table of contents
1) Scope and owners
2) Systems & services inventory (high level)
3) Dashboards & alerting standards
4) Runbooks & incident playbooks
5) How-tos and common procedures
6) Recent retrospectives & action items
7) Q4 roadmap and milestones
8) Contacts and escalation

1) Scope and owners
- Scope: All production-facing platform systems including API gateway, routing layer, GPU inference scheduler, KV caching service, telemetry pipeline (Prometheus -> Cortex -> Grafana), alerting (Alertmanager), and the platform control plane services (deploy, config, rollout).
- Primary owners: platform-systems (pager), infra-telemetry (metrics & dashboards), serving-runtime (model runtime owners for GPU services).
- Service owner table (short):
  - api-gateway: owner=platform-systems-team, oncall=platform-pager
  - inference-scheduler: owner=eng-serving-runtime, oncall=serving-pager
  - kv-cache: owner=platform-services, oncall=platform-pager
  - telemetry-pipeline: owner=eng-platform, oncall=telemetry-pager

2) Systems & services inventory (high level)
| Service | Purpose | SLO | Primary metric | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| api-gateway | ingress + routing + auth | 99.95% availability | 5xx rate, p95 latency | platform-systems
| inference-scheduler | model assignment + GPU packing | 99.9% request-accepted | queue length, reject rate | eng-serving-runtime
| kv-cache | prefix/KV caching across instances | 99.5% hit-rate | cache hit ratio | platform-services
| telemetry-pipeline | collect/route metrics & logs | 99% data-availability | scrape success %, ingestion lag | eng-platform

3) Dashboards & alerting standards
- Dashboard naming convention: platform.<service>.<purpose> (e.g., platform.inference-scheduler.health). Keep a one-line description in dashboard metadata.
- Required dashboards per service: Overview (latency, error rate, throughput), Capacity (resource utilization, queue length), Cost (GPU utilization, per-token cost proxy for inference), Reliability (SLO burn-down).
- Alerting rule tiers:
  - P0 (page): immediate pager. Conditions: service down, sustained >5xx threshold (>=1% of traffic for 1m across PODs), SLO burn >50% in 5m window.
  - P1 (page during business hours): degraded latency (p95 > configured threshold + 20% for 5m), queue pressure (queue length > 75% of configured capacity for 10m).
  - P2 (ticket): non-urgent capacity warnings, config drift warnings.

Example Prometheus alert (copy into repo /infra/monitoring/alerts/platform-inference.yaml):

alert: InferenceSchedulerHighQueueLength
expr: inference_scheduler_queue_length{job="inference-scheduler"} > 800
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Inference scheduler queue length > 800 for 10m"

Alert routing and runbook links must be included in Alertmanager config with team labels (team=serving-runtime, team=platform). Use incident templates to pre-populate Slack channel and runbook link.

4) Runbooks & incident playbooks
- Structure for every runbook: symptom, impact, immediate mitigation, triage checks, rollback/mitigation steps, postmortem checklist, owner. Keep runbooks under /runbooks and name: <service>-<incident-type>-runbook.

Example: inference-scheduler-unhealthy-runbook (summary)
1) Symptom: new incoming requests rejected with 503 and scheduler logs show OOMs or heavy GC.
2) Impact: client requests fail, downstream queuing increases, user visible errors.
3) Immediate mitigation (ordered):
   a) Route traffic to fallback model variant via routing policy (console -> routes -> set fallback).
   b) Scale inference-scheduler horizontally: kubectl scale deployment inference-scheduler --replicas=<+2>.
   c) If due to OOM, restart offending pods one by one: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker --field-selector=status.phase=Running.
4) Triage checks:
   - Check pod logs: kubectl logs -n prod deployment/inference-scheduler -c scheduler --tail=200
   - Check metrics: p95 latency, reject rate, GPU memory utilization
5) Post-incident: run mem/heap profiling, capture flamegraph, open regression ticket against model change or config.

5) How-tos and common procedures
- Oncall handover: Fill daily handover doc (template path: /templates/oncall-handover.md) and post to #oncall-bridge. Include open incidents and paging history.
- Add dashboard: clone template dashboard, update Prometheus queries, add owners metadata. Submit PR to infra/monitoring/dashboards and link to related runbook.
- Add alert: write alert rule, include clear remediation steps in annotation, tag with team label, and add to Alertmanager routing. Include a test query and runbook link in the annotation.
- Release and rollout: follow rollout playbook: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15m observation windows and automated rollback on SLO violation. Use rollout tool: redwoodctl rollout create --service <svc> --canary=5 --observe=15m

6) Recent retrospectives & action items
- Retro 2026-09-21: "Increased inference tail latency after kernel update"
  - Findings: new CUDA kernel delivered uneven memory pressure leading to GC spikes on small-batch workloads.
  - Actions: add additional mem headroom in scheduler, update kernel test harness, add p95 GPU memory metric to canary dashboards. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Luis Ortega). ETA: 2026-11-15 (in progress).
- Retro 2026-10-05: "Alert storm during telemetry migration"
  - Findings: missing dedup rules in Alertmanager and dubious thresholds.
  - Actions: add dedup labels, introduce rate-limited paging for noisy alerts, review thresholds with telemetry team. Owner: eng-platform (Maya Patel). Completed: 2026-10-27.

7) Q4 roadmap and milestones (high level)
- Oct-Nov: Alert rationalization sprint - reduce noisy alerts by 40%; roll out new alert templates. Owner: eng-platform.
- Nov: Dashboard migration to unified Grafana folders and standard metadata. Owner: infra-telemetry.
- Nov-Dec: Inference scheduler autoscaler v2 - better GPU packing, preemptive draining for upgrades. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Dec: Runbook coverage goal - 95% of P0/P1 alerts have an associated runbook link in Alertmanager. Owner: platform-ops.

8) Contacts and escalation
- Primary oncall rotation: #platform-oncall (Slack) - paged by Alertmanager.
- Emergency pager escalation: platform-pager -> platform-rotation-lead -> VP of Engineering. Escalation timeline: 0m (page), 10m (escalate to rotation lead), 30m (escalate to director).
- Postmortem owner assignment: the oncall at time of incident is responsible for the interim write-up within 72 hours. Full postmortem (with blameless timeline and action items) due in 7 days.

Appendix - useful commands and links
- kubectl logs -n prod deployment/<service> -c <container> --tail=500
- redwoodctl rollout status --service <service> --watch
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com (folder: platform/<team>)
- Alertmanager config: https://git.internal.redwood.com/infra/monitoring/tree/main/alertmanager.yaml

Maintenance notes
- Keep this page up to date: make a small change whenever a new dashboard or runbook is merged. Major roadmap changes require an owner update and a short summary at the top.

If you find missing services or outdated runbooks, please add a PR to the wiki repo and notify #platform-docs.
